data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1. The finite obstruction structures are locally stable mixed configurations in which the crossing edges form a matching: each vertex has at most one neighbor of the opposite color. The prevalence of these obstructions in the final state scales as Theta(sqrt(n)) crossing edges with high probability, while the probability of the empty matching, i.e. consensus, converges to a constant c in (0,1).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The constant is 0 if the branching process is subcritical for all initial densities.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The constant is 1 if the branching process almost surely consumes all edges.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The law fails if expansion creates linear-sized jammed matchings that dominate the final state.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The law fails if degree-3 vertices are not negligible in the critical window.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Let H be the number of bichromatic edges. A vertex flips only if it has 2 or 3 opposite-color neighbors, and each flip reduces H by 1 or 3, so H is a Lyapunov function. Stable mixed states are exactly those whose crossing edges form a matching. The mean-field ODE dp/dt = -2p^2 drives the crossing density to p ~ 1/sqrt(n), where H = Theta(sqrt(n)) and the remaining degree-2 vertices form a critical branching process. The survival probability of this branching process is the constant probability of eliminating all crossing edges.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
